The Business Problem: The $180 Sneaker Dilemma

The Retail Balancing Act

Apex Athletics footwear buyers and regional distribution center planners face a high-stakes operational dilemma:

  • Capital vs. Service Level: Carrying excess safety stock strains working capital, while lean inventory risks catastrophic stockouts.
  • Forecasting Vacuum: Planners often rely on intuitive guesswork or static historical averages that fail to anticipate demand inflections.
  • Operational Dependency: Purchasing, warehouse staging, and hourly reorder schedules all depend directly on forward sales expectations.
  • The Core Need: High-fidelity, monthly forecasting models paired with an automated decision framework to prescribe exact reorder quantities.

📦 Dilemma A: Overstocking

Consequence: Trapped Capital in Shoe Boxes

  • Cash flow restricted in slow-moving warehouse shoe boxes
  • Elevated storage, insurance, and handling costs
  • Forced 40% margin erosion through post-holiday clearance markdowns

⚠️ Dilemma B: Understocking

Consequence: Stockouts on Black Friday

  • Immediate loss of sales when popular sneaker sizes run out
  • Permanent customer defection to competitors
  • Emergency freight costs and supply chain disruption

🎯 The Project Objective

Provide Apex footwear buyers with a scenario-aware forecasting tool to automate factory replenishment orders.

"At the heart of Apex Athletics is a classic high-stakes retail dilemma: inventory replenishment. Consider a flagship $180 running sneaker. If our central buyers understock ahead of the December holiday rush, customers walk out of our stores and buy from competitors down the street—that revenue is lost forever. But if we overstock, thousands of shoe boxes sit in our regional distribution centers, tying up vital cash and forcing painful 40% clearance markdowns in February. Compounding this, our factories require a 4-to-6 week lead time for production and overseas shipping. To optimize this balance, Apex needed a reliable forecasting and reorder system."

Target & Exogenous Logic

Target (RSAFS): Captures actual U.S. consumer dollar turnover.
Exogenous Context: Sentiment measures willingness to spend, while CPI captures price pressure. Resampled to Month-Start (MS) with forward-fill for alignment without lookahead bias.

Macroeconomic Drivers: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (Blue) vs. CPI (Red) across 2012–2026.
"To build a robust top-down forecasting model, we utilized the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) U.S. Retail Sales dataset (RSAFS) across 176 months from January 2012 to August 2026. Because athletic footwear is a discretionary consumer purchase, category sales closely track overall national retail velocity. To enhance our predictive power, we incorporated two crucial macroeconomic variables: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment, capturing consumer willingness to spend on discretionary apparel, and the Consumer Price Index (CPI), reflecting how inflation squeezes household budgets."

Exploratory Data Analysis: Key Insights

U.S. Retail Sales (RSAFS): Sustained secular upward expansion with sharp March-April 2020 COVID-19 contraction.

Key EDA Observations

  • Secular Trend: Total volume grew from \$350B (2012) to \$720B+ (2026).
  • COVID Shock & V-Recovery: Extreme 2-month plunge followed by stimulus-fueled rapid recovery.
Multiplicative Seasonal Decomposition: Highlights invariant 12-month December holiday cycle and residual variance concentration.

Seasonal Structure

  • December Peak: Predictable +15–20% holiday spending volume spike.
  • January Valley: Consistent post-holiday inventory contraction.
"Our exploratory data analysis revealed patterns that match footwear retail reality. First, retail demand exhibits a strong, persistent upward trend. Second, seasonality is extreme: we see massive spikes every December for holiday shopping, alongside a secondary bump in August for back-to-school footwear. The clearest anomaly is the sudden COVID-19 dip and sharp recovery in 2020. Our seasonal decomposition confirmed that annual footwear demand follows a consistent cyclical rhythm, making it an ideal candidate for time series modeling."

Modeling Methodology & Validation Strategy

Temporal Integrity & Rigorous Splitting

  • Strict Time-Based Split:
    • Training Window: 164 Months (Jan 2012 – Aug 2025)
    • Hold-Out Test Window: Final 12 Months (Sep 2025 – Aug 2026)
  • Zero Lookahead Bias: Absolutely no random shuffling was used. Future data was locked away to realistically emulate forward planning.
  • Evaluation Standards: Evaluated strictly on out-of-sample hold-out predictions using Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE).
  • Benchmark Standard: Evaluated against a rigorous Seasonal Naïve baseline (yt = yt-12) representing the classic "same-month-last-year" retail heuristic.

Candidate Architectures Tested:
1. Seasonal Naïve (Baseline) • 2. Holt-Winters Exponential Smoothing • 3. Univariate SARIMA • 4. SARIMAX with Exogenous Macro Drivers.

Chronological Split: 164-Month Training Window (Blue) vs. 12-Month Out-of-Sample Holdout (Orange).
"To evaluate our models realistically, we maintained a strict time-based split. We trained on the first 164 months and reserved the final 12 months as an out-of-sample holdout test set. We strictly avoided random shuffling to prevent any future data leakage. We benchmarked against a Seasonal Naïve model—which simply repeats the prior year's monthly figures—and tested three candidate models: Holt-Winters Additive Exponential Smoothing, a univariate SARIMA, and a multivariate SARIMAX incorporating inflation and consumer sentiment."

🏆 Strategic Decision Rationale

  • 80.0% Error Reduction: SARIMAX slashes prediction error by four-fifths compared to the Seasonal Naïve baseline.
  • Operational Superiority: While Holt-Winters achieves slightly lower holdout RMSE, it is purely univariate. SARIMAX unlocks dynamic macroeconomic scenario testing (inflation shifts, consumer sentiment dips), providing vastly higher business decision value.
12-Month Out-of-Sample Holdout: SARIMAX (Blue) tracks actual sales (Black) tightly across seasonal peaks.
"Looking at our test results, Holt-Winters delivered impressive statistical accuracy with an RMSE of 4,707. However, Holt-Winters is a univariate model—it cannot see inflation or consumer sentiment. For Apex Athletics, we strategically selected the multivariate SARIMAX model. Even though its RMSE is slightly higher at 5,778, it still achieves an 80% error reduction over the baseline. Most importantly, it gives our buyers the superpower to run 'what-if' scenario simulations, adjusting purchase orders if inflation spikes or consumer confidence wavers."

Residual Diagnostics: Statistical Rigor & Limitations

Diagnostic Test Evaluation

  • Formal Ljung-Box Autocorrelation Test:
    • Lag 12: p = 0.0101 (Marginally significant residual correlation remaining at seasonal cycle)
    • Lag 24: p = 0.2788 (Fails to reject null hypothesis; no significant long-term autocorrelation)
  • White Noise Validation: The SARIMAX specification successfully extracts trend and annual seasonality, converting the series into near-ideal stationary noise.
  • Transparent Limitation (COVID Shock): The 4-panel diagnostic plot demonstrates that residual volatility is almost entirely concentrated in the March–May 2020 pandemic lockdown shock. Under standard macroeconomic cycles, residuals conform closely to normality.

Model Health Verdict: Validated for forward planning, with caution advised during macroeconomic black swan events.

4-Panel Diagnostics: Residuals over time, distribution vs. KDE, 24-lag ACF, and Normal Q-Q plot.
"To rigorously validate our selected model, we examined residual diagnostics. The Ljung-Box test at lag 24 yields a p-value of 0.28, indicating that our model successfully extracts temporal structure and leaves white noise. While lag 12 shows minor autocorrelation (p=0.01), our diagnostic plots confirm this is almost entirely concentrated around the unprecedented 2020 pandemic lockdown. For normal planning conditions, the model is statistically sound and highly reliable."

Live Prototype Demo: Interactive Reorder Tool

Streamlit Application Workflow

  • Interactive Scenario Planning (Sidebar):
    • Dynamic sliders allow managers to adjust expected shifts in Inflation (CPI ±5%) and Consumer Sentiment (±20%) across a 6-month horizon.
    • Pickled SARIMAX engine recalculates dynamic point forecasts and confidence bands on the fly.
  • Store-Level Inventory Inputs:
    • Current warehouse stock on hand (e.g., 50,000 pairs)
    • Safety stock buffer percentage (e.g., 15%)
    • Supplier lead time (1–8 weeks) & Planning horizon (1–6 months)
  • Automated Decision Statement:
    • Calculates Reorder Point: ROP = (Demand / Weeks) × Lead Time + Safety Stock
    • Outputs explicit purchasing actions and replenishment recommendations.

Limitations & Future Engineering Roadmap

⚠️ Current System Limitations

  • Macroeconomic Black Swans: Statistical time series models struggle with structural breaks and exogenous shocks (e.g., pandemic shutdowns, war-induced supply bottlenecks).
  • Flat Shift Assumption: Prototype sliders assume uniform percentage shifts across all 6 horizon months rather than dynamic month-by-month trajectories.
  • Deterministic Lead Times: Order formulas currently treat lead times and demand rates as fixed, whereas real retail faces stochastic supplier delays.
  • Macro Aggregation: U.S. aggregate retail sales (FRED RSAFS) masks regional variance and micro-market shifts.

🚀 Production Roadmap & Enhancements

  • Category-Level Decomposition: Expand beyond aggregate RSAFS into distinct category sub-models (e.g., Apparel vs. Groceries vs. Consumer Electronics).
  • Real-Time POS Integration: Connect live REST APIs to store Point-of-Sale (POS) and ERP systems (SAP, Oracle) for real-time stock sync.
  • Automated Alerting Engine: Implement automated email and webhook notifications triggered when stock falls below calculated safety buffers.
  • Multi-Horizon Optimization: Integrate dynamic Bayesian updating to adjust forecast confidence intervals as new weekly sales receipts clear.
"We also want to be transparent about limitations and future enhancements. Currently, our prototype forecasts at the aggregate footwear category level and assumes scenario shifts hold steady across the horizon. For an enterprise rollout at Apex Athletics, our next phase would introduce SKU and shoe-size curve allocation—breaking down orders into specific sizes like 9.5 or 11. We would also integrate directly with our overseas suppliers via EDI for automated purchase order routing."

Questions & Discussion

Thank you for your time and engagement!

Q1: Why SARIMAX over Prophet / Deep Learning?

Statistical state-space models are transparent, mathematically rigorous, and fast to re-estimate while natively ingesting exogenous macroeconomic regressors without overfitting on 176 monthly observations.

Q2: Why not Holt-Winters with lower RMSE?

Holt-Winters is strictly univariate. SARIMAX achieves an 80% improvement over benchmark while enabling scenario simulation with inflation and sentiment shifts.

Q3: How does an Apex footwear buyer use this?

Planners enter current backroom inventory, select expected macro conditions, and instantly receive exact purchase order quantities and replenishment recommendations.
